sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: Psychiatric crises, such as a relapse of psychosis, may be associated with reduced decision-making capability [1].
label: none

sentence: In the United Kingdom (UK), health service users have the right under the Mental Capacity Act (MCA) 2005 to make an informed advance treatment refusal [2] when capacitous, regarding times when their decision-making capability is impaired.
label: none

sentence: Advance refusals are legally binding, but may be overridden if the patient is subject to an involuntary treatment order under the Mental Health Act 1983, amended 2007 (MHA).
label: none

sentence: People subject to the MHA are given reasons for their detention and their rights are explained at the point of detention.
label: none

sentence: In the case of advance refusals, an appropriate point at which to inform service users of the legal right to make such a refusal and help them to exercise it is during the process of crisis planning for mental health care.
label: none

sentence: In the national Health Service (NHS) mental health services in England, a written crisis plan is routinely present in the care plan, and is written and updated through the Care Programme Approach (CPA) [3].
label: none

sentence: This provides the current benchmark for written crisis plans.
label: none

sentence: An audit of CPA forms showed very few documented refusals, at just 2.4% of a sample of 424 crisis plans [4].
label: none

sentence: In contrast, studies of both facilitated psychiatric advance directives (f-PADs) in the US [5, 6] and Joint Crisis Plans (JCPs) in the UK [7, 8] show much higher rates of refusals, at around three quarters of participants completing a f-PAD [5] or JCP [8].
label: none

sentence: These are structured research interventions in which an independent mental health professional facilitates a discussion about preferences for future care - including treatment refusals - with the service user and, in the case of the JCP, with professionals involved in his or her care [9].
label: none

sentence: The discrepancy between these interventions and routine care plans suggests that if service users are given better information about their rights, more would make advance refusals.
label: none

sentence: However, the previous studies in the UK occurred before the MCA 2005 was introduced, so it is not clear whether the situation concerning refusals has changed.
label: none

sentence: One trial conducted since the introduction of the MCA 2005 of JCPs for outpatients with borderline personality disorder [10] showed a very high (90.2%) rate of refusals, but no comparison with the rate of refusals in the conventional treatment plan was made.
label: none

sentence: We therefore made use of data from a recent multisite trial of JCPs [11–13] that incorporated and explained the relevant provision in the MCA.
label: none

sentence: Our first aim was to ascertain whether - and to what extent - the JCP process elicited more written advance treatment refusals than the CPA process during the process of a pragmatic randomised controlled trial.
label: none

sentence: Our second aim was to explore the nature of such refusals and the relationships between making a refusal with service user characteristics.
label: none

sentence: To address the first aim we tested the hypothesis that the rate of refusals would be higher in JCPs than in CPA treatment plans.
label: none

sentence: To address the second aim we tested the following hypotheses: (1) the majority of refusals will be accepted by clinicians without concerns that they will reduce the standard of care provided/received [6]; (2) refusals are more likely to be made by participants who either a) have prior experience of coercion i.e.
label: none

sentence: transport or detention under the Mental Health Act; b) report a high level of perceived coercion at baseline; or c) report poor working alliance with professionals at baseline.
label: none

sentence: All of these factors may indicate a lack of acceptance of at least some aspects of treatment and hence a wish to avoid these treatment components in future.
label: none

sentence: Methods
label: none

sentence: Setting and sample
label: none

sentence: The sample for this study is a sub-sample from the CRIMSON trial [11–13].
label: none

sentence: The CRIMSON trial was a multi-site randomised controlled trial of JCPs for individuals with psychotic disorders in four mental health Trusts (NHS service provider organisations) in the UK (total n = 569).
label: none

sentence: The eligibility criteria for the CRIMSON trial were: diagnosis of a psychotic disorder; admission to a psychiatric ward in the last two years and current contact with a community mental health team.
label: none

sentence: Service users who were in hospital or under a section of the Mental Health Act at the time of recruitment were deemed ineligible so as to avoid any potential perceived coercion to participate.
label: none

sentence: No other exclusions were made, thus maximising generalisability.
label: none

sentence: This study uses data from three overlapping study samples: (1) intervention group participants who completed the JCP process (n = 221) and whose JCP could therefore be assessed for refusals; and (2) the 424 patients whose CPA care plans were available for assessment for treatment refusals at baseline; and (3) those in the control group whose CPA care plans were available at baseline and follow up (n = 221).
label: none

sentence: The intervention
label: none

sentence: The JCP [7, 14] was developed in the later 1990’s.
label: none

sentence: The starting point was a review of existing models containing information about the service user and requests for treatment during a relapse or crisis [14].
label: none

sentence: Sections were then added to encourage reflection about past crises that would help inform the thinking and planning for future crises.
label: none

sentence: Headings were included where circumstances or triggers for past relapses could be recorded, as well as details of early signs of relapse and space to record both the good and bad aspects of care received during previous crises.
label: none

sentence: These headings precede the advance planning section so that during the meeting to finalise the plan these aspects are discussed.
label: none

sentence: Eliciting this information promotes a process of shared decision making at the planning meeting, as the treating clinicians are present and can also share their observations of early warning signs, triggers, and what has been helpful/not helpful in the past [15].
label: none

sentence: The completed JCP contains the service user’s statements about past treatment and preferences for care in the event of a future relapse or crisis.
label: none

sentence: It was produced after two meetings.
label: none

sentence: At the first meeting, the JCP facilitator - a member of the research team independent of the clinical team - explained the procedure to the service user and the care coordinator.
label: none

sentence: To finalise each plan, the service user was encouraged to bring a carer, friend, or advocate to a second meeting.
label: none

sentence: The aim of this meeting was to discuss the views of the service user, his or her informal supports(s) and treating professionals regarding what to do in a future crisis, and to negotiate agreed solutions.
label: none

sentence: The JCP facilitator’s role was to ensure that everyone’s perspective was heard but the final choice of what was included in the plan (including the exact terminology used) lay with the service user.
label: none

sentence: The clinical team was present to discuss options and the implications of the service user’s choice.
label: none

sentence: When the option of stating which treatment(s) they did not want to receive in future was discussed, the facilitator explained the MCA 2005 provision for making a treatment refusal.
label: none

sentence: All JCPs were written in the first person to reflect the service user’s own description of their mental health issue and wishes for treatment.
label: none

sentence: At the end of this meeting the JCP facilitator asked clinicians if they were happy to agree to the overall plan, in order to clarify to the service user any content that they thought could not be followed and have this acknowledged on the JCP.
label: none

sentence: After finalising the JCP, service users were given a copy and an electronic version of the plan was stored on the Trust’s electronic patient record system.
label: none

sentence: Once completed, the content of the JCP could be updated by service user and the regular clinical team and used in routine care planning.
label: none

sentence: The intervention group received the JCP intervention in addition to treatment as usual (described below).
label: none

sentence: As the unit of randomisation was the service user, some individual care coordinators and individual doctors may have developed more than one JCP.
label: none

sentence: Likewise, some individual care coordinators and doctors may have had service users in both the control and intervention groups.
label: none

sentence: Treatment as usual control
label: none

sentence: The control condition was Treatment As Usual as stipulated under the CPA.
label: none

sentence: Treatment As Usual under the CPA includes requirements that all service users are assessed, receive a written care plan that includes a crisis and contingency plan, and that this is reviewed regularly.
label: none

sentence: In most situations, service users have a nominated Care Coordinator, whose role is to be the central point for communication regarding the service user and to ensure the service user’s identified health and social care needs are met.
label: none

sentence: Treatment As Usual thus in theory allows the making of refusals and their documentation on the CPA form by the Care Coordinator, although the form may not specifically prompt them to do so.
label: none

sentence: Thus, the control condition not only lacks the process of facilitation but also depends on existing documentation required by the service.
label: none

sentence: Assessments
label: none

sentence: Assessment for treatment refusals and whether clinicians would not be able to follow them: Refusals were assessed in both the JCPs and CPA care plans.
label: none

sentence: A content analysis of the JCPs was conducted by SF.
label: none

sentence: Refusals were coded as present or not present, and content of refusals was thematically coded [16].
label: none

sentence: For refusals on the CPA care plan, the entire CPA care plan was printed and anonymised by research assistants.
label: none

sentence: SF assessed the content of each plan at baseline and follow-up for the presence of treatment refusals and for the presence of statements by clinicians about any aspect of the JCP that they thought could not be followed/adhered to.
label: none

sentence: Demographics: Research assistants collected demographic data from service users and Care Coordinators including age, sex, ethnicity, education/qualification and number of years in contact with mental health services.
label: none

sentence: For Care Coordinators, length of psychiatric practice and length of relationship with the service user were also collected.
label: none

sentence: Hospitalisations: Data regarding psychiatric admissions in the two years prior to baseline and over the follow-up period including duration and admission status (formal/informal) were collected by research assistants from routine Trust data sets and corroborated by service users and clinicians at interview.
label: none

sentence: Self-harm and harm to others: At baseline interview participants were asked about instances and severity of self-harm, suicide attempts and harm to others in the two years prior to baseline and, at follow-up, they were asked about the period since baseline assessment (usually 18 months).
label: none

sentence: Objective Coercion: use of the Mental Health Act to transport the service user or detain them in a psychiatric unit.
label: none

sentence: Perceived Coercion: was measured by the perceived coercion subscale of the service user self-report measure the MacArthur Perceived Coercion Scale [17], adapted for use in outpatient treatment.
label: none

sentence: Higher scores indicate more perceived coercion.
label: none

sentence: Therapeutic Relationships: The Working Alliance Inventory short form (WAI-S) [18, 19] modified for use in psychiatric samples [20] was rated by service users and clinicians (WAIC and WAIT respectively) at baseline and follow-up.
label: none

sentence: Engagement: was measured by the Service Engagement Scale (SES) [21].
label: none

sentence: This is a 14-item scale producing four subscales measuring ‘availability’, ‘collaboration’, ‘help seeking’ and ‘treatment adherence’ and a total score.
label: none

sentence: Higher scores on this measure indicate poorer engagement.
label: none

sentence: This measure was rated by the Care Coordinator.
label: none

sentence: Data analysis
label: none

sentence: To assess the proportion of refusals not identified through the CPA process we compared the proportion of refusals in the 221 completed JCPs with that in CPA forms available: (1) at baseline for the entire group (n = 424); and (2) at follow-up for the control group only (n = 203), as the presence or absence of a refusal in a JCP could influence whether it was present in the participants’ CPA form at follow-up.
label: none

sentence: The analyses aimed at identifying factors associated with refusals were restricted to the JCP group as it was only in this group that there was a sufficient number.
label: none

sentence: Associations between covariates and missing data regarding treatment refusal were investigated using chi-squared and t-tests as appropriate.
label: none

sentence: Covariates found to be associated with missing data were accounted for in all analyses.
label: none

sentence: Chi-squared analyses and t-tests were performed to ascertain any relationships between making a refusal and baseline service user clinical or demographic characteristics based on bivariate analysis.
label: none

sentence: The hypothesised factors associated with a refusal were: previous compulsory admissions, perceived coercion and service user-rated working alliance at baseline.
label: none

sentence: These were regressed on an indicator of refusal of treatment using logistic regression.
label: none

sentence: The logistic regression model was adjusted for covariates associated with missing information or treatment refusal.
label: none

sentence: Results
label: none

sentence: Rates of refusals in the CPA forms versus JCPs
label: none

sentence: Of the total sample for the CRIMSON trial (n = 569, 284 control, 285 intervention), 424 (74%) CPA forms were available (221 controls and 203 intervention).
label: none

sentence: We were unable to obtain records from one Trust (n = 48).
label: none

sentence: The remainder were missing due to: not being able to locate a care plan at baseline or follow-up (n = 52); participants being discharged at follow-up (n = 22) or downgraded to care support and thus no care plan (n = 8); deaths (n = 5); and refusing access to records (n = 10).
label: none

sentence: Ten of these 424 CPA forms (2.4%) included refusals at baseline.
label: none

sentence: For the control group, six of the 221 (2.7%, 95% CI 1.0%–5.8%) included a refusal at follow-up on their CPA forms.
label: none

sentence: In the intervention group 221/285 (77%) completed a JCP.
label: none

sentence: Of these, 99 (45%, 95% CI 38%–52%) made a refusal as part of the JCP.
label: none

sentence: Agreements with JCPs by clinicians
label: none

sentence: There were no cases where clinicians explicitly disagreed with the final version of the JCP.
label: none

sentence: Types of refusal
label: none

sentence: Based on the JCP sample, the most common refusal was regarding aspects of medication: 45/99 (45%) made a refusal of a specific medication (with 53% of this subsample providing a reason for this refusal); 20/99 (20%) refused injections.
label: none

sentence: Others made refusals regarding high doses of medication, increases or changes to dose.
label: none

sentence: Only one participant stated that they would prefer not to take any medication.
label: none

sentence: Seventeen refusals regarding specific medications were made: one anti-cholinergic, three different mood stabilisers, two anti-depressants, one anti-anxiolytic and ten anti-psychotics.
label: none

sentence: The most frequently refused anti-psychotics were: haloperidol (n = 9), olanzapine (n = 8), risperidone (n = 5), zuclopenthixol (n = 5), quetiapine (n = 4) and chlorpromazine (n = 4).
label: none

sentence: The next most common category of refusal was electro-convulsive therapy (ECT; 19/99 (19%).
label: none

sentence: Eighteen participants (18%) made refusals relating to admission to hospital.
label: none

sentence: Of these, eight (44%) made refusals about specific aspects of admission, such as which ward they were admitted to.
label: none

sentence: The remaining ten (56%) refused hospital admission, though seven added a caveat, for example, “[I refuse] being put in hospital.
label: none

sentence: I know that this is sometimes necessary however I would like this to be the last resort”.
label: none

sentence: While these caveats reflect acknowledgements of the views of clinicians, there was no indication on the other three as to whether clinicians disagreed with these refusals.
label: none

sentence: Predictors of refusal
label: none

sentence: Sixty-four (22%) of participants in the JCP arm did not complete a JCP.
label: none

sentence: These participants were similar in most respects to those who did, but tended to have had more psychiatric admissions in the two years prior to the trial, have a higher engagement with care (SES) score and higher clinician-rated working alliance (WAIT).
label: none

sentence: We therefore adjusted further analyses for the number of admissions, SES and WAIT score to account for bias due to missing data.
label: none

sentence: Table 1 Description of the JCP sample at baseline by refusal status.
label: none

sentence: Table 1 describes the sample with JCP refusal information by refusal status.
label: none

sentence: Treatment refusal was individually associated with the participant’s location, ethnicity, years in contact with mental health services and the perceived coercion subscale of the McArthur coercion scale before adjustments.
label: none

sentence: There was no bivariate association between having had an involuntary admission in the two years prior to baseline assessment or service user-rated working alliance and treatment refusal.
label: none

sentence: Table 2 Hypothesised baseline predictors of treatment refusal within the JCP treatment arm, adjusted for covariates listed, n = 168.
label: none

sentence: Logistic regression of the refusal status on the three hypothesised baseline predictors (involuntary admission, perceived coercion and therapeutic alliance) adjusting for site, ethnicity, contact with services and covariates associated with missingness (SES, number of admissions and carer-rated working alliance) are provided in Table 2.
label: none

sentence: The results indicate that there is no association between working alliance or involuntary admission and advance treatment refusals.
label: none

sentence: The association between perceived coercion and advance refusals remains significant when other factors are accounted for (odds ratio = 1.34, 95% CI 1.07–1.69, p = 0.013).
label: none

sentence: Table 2 also shows that participant location remains associated with advance refusals after adjustment for other factors.
label: none

sentence: Discussion
label: none

sentence: Summary of findings
label: none

sentence: Comparison of the rates of advance refusals made in JCPs with those made in CPA forms among trial participants shows that the potential demand for refusals is barely addressed by the current CPA process used in routine care.
label: none

sentence: Our results also suggest that most refusals made using the JCP were not out of keeping with what the clinicians viewed as safe clinical practice.
label: none

sentence: In no cases did clinicians attending the JCP meetings disagree with the refusals made, although it should be noted that this does not mean all refusals were then followed in practice.
label: none

sentence: It is also possible that clinicians did not voice their concerns during the meetings (despite being asked for their views by the facilitator), as suggested by qualitative interviews of some participating clinicians [22].
label: none

sentence: They may instead have wanted to avoid an argument with the service user and/or have judged the process to be non-binding.
label: none

sentence: Thus, knowing that refusals made under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 can be overridden using the Mental Health Act may reduce the attention paid by clinicians to refusals made by serviced users, despite the possibility of honouring a refusal (such as that of a particular medication) while someone is detained under the Mental Health Act.
label: none

sentence: Among those who received a JCP, higher perceived coercion at baseline was associated with subsequent treatment refusal, as hypothesised.
label: none

sentence: However, no association was found with having a previous involuntary admission or working alliance and subsequent treatment refusal.
label: none

sentence: The association with duration of contact with mental health services, along with the lack of association with involuntary admission or working alliance, suggests that many refusals are made based on experiences of treatments regardless of whether these were experienced while detained under the Mental Health Act.
label: none

sentence: Participant location at the sites outside London was also associated with treatment refusal.
label: none

sentence: This may indicate differences in implementation of the JCP development process among the sites on the part of the facilitators, despite the provision of supervision of all facilitators by the same member of the research team.
label: none

sentence: A second possibility is the existence of site level differences in participants’ past experiences of treatment, which were not captured in the assessment and exclude use of the Mental Health Act per se, but which give rise to higher rates of treatment refusal.
label: none

sentence: Limitations of the study
label: none

sentence: While the JCP intervention allowed us to assess demand for treatment refusals and their relationship with clinical and demographic factors, the sample was subject to the eligibility criteria for the CRIMSON trial.
label: limitation

sentence: This took place in three urban and one rural area within the three sites and included only those with an admission in the last two years; the sample is therefore not fully representative of adults with psychoses using secondary mental health services in England.
label: limitation

sentence: Further, we are unable to report the extent to which refusals were honoured due to the CRIMSON trial resource limitations.
label: limitation

sentence: Conclusions
label: none

sentence: Our findings are consistent with previous research showing there is strong demand for psychiatric advance statements [23–25] and that the content of most advance statements can be followed without compromising care [6, 25, 26].
label: none

sentence: However, most of those who want to make a statement need support to complete it [5, 27], and despite the existence of UK legislation for advance refusals, services offer no systematic or efficient way of providing this support.
label: none

sentence: We have thus highlighted an aspect of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 which has been under-implemented in mental health services.
label: none

sentence: The creation of, access to, and honouring of individualised crisis plans which include refusals are important in their own right but are missing from current care pathways [4].
label: none

sentence: The research evidence is clear that interventions such as Joint Crisis Plans and facilitated psychiatric advance directives are an effective way to inform service users of their legal rights to make advance treatment refusals; they probably also improve working alliance with clinicians [13, 24].
label: none

sentence: Evidence that these interventions can lead to ‘harder’ outcomes such as reduced use of involuntary treatment [28] and for their cost-effectiveness [12, 29] is more mixed, and may reflect problems in implementation.11 However, a recent systematic review identified advance statements as the only intervention associated with reduction in the use of compulsory treatment [28].
label: none

sentence: Further work is needed to identify ways to overcome barriers to the creation of advance statements, together with study of the outcomes associated with not just their creation but of their application in routine practice.
label: none

sentence: Recently arguments have been presented that involuntary detention and treatment under mental health legislation be like that for general health care, that is, based on impaired decision-making capacity and best interests [30].
label: none

sentence: In such a case, a treatment refusal could not be ‘trumped’ by mental health legislation.
label: none

sentence: If the law were to be reformed, the patient’s decision-making capacity would need to be assured, especially when a treatment refusal with serious health consequences was desired.
label: none

sentence: The place of a state’s duty to protect life, as under the European Convention on Human Rights, might need to be considered.
label: none

sentence: The impact of legal reform on the implementation of support for service users to make advance statements, which may include refusals, is not clear.
label: none

sentence: Socio-demographic determinants and effect of structured personal diabetes care: a 19-year follow-up of the randomized controlled study diabetes Care in General Practice (DCGP)
label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: We investigated how four aspects of socio-demography influence the effectiveness of an intervention with structured personal diabetes care on long-term outcomes.
label: none

sentence: Methods
label: none

sentence: The Diabetes Care in General Practice (DCGP) study is a cluster-randomized trial involving a population-based sample of 1381 patients with newly diagnosed type 2-diabetes mellitus.
label: none

sentence: We investigated how education, employment, cohabitation status and residence influenced the effectiveness of 6 years of intervention with structured personal diabetes care, resembling present day recommendations.
label: none

sentence: Outcomes were incidence of any diabetes-related endpoint and death during 19 years after diagnosis, and cardiovascular risk factors, behaviour, attitudes and process-of-care variables 6 years after diagnosis.
label: none

sentence: Results
label: none

sentence: Structured personal care reduced the risk of any diabetes-related endpoint and the effect of the intervention was modified by geographical area (interaction p = 0.034) with HR of 0.71 (95%CI: 0.60–0.85) and of 1.07 (95%CI: 0.77–1.48), for patients in urban and rural areas, respectively.
label: none

sentence: Otherwise, there was no effect modification of education, employment and civil status on the intervention for the final endpoints.
label: none

sentence: There were no noticeable socio-demographic differences in the effect of the intervention on cardiovascular risk factors, behaviour, attitudes, and process-of-care.
label: none

sentence: Conclusion
label: none

sentence: Structured personal care reduced the aggregate outcome of any diabetes-related endpoint and independent of socio-demographic factors similar effect on cardiovascular risk factors, behaviour, attitudes and process of care, but the intervention did not change the existing inequity in mortality and morbidity.
label: none

sentence: Residence modified the uptake of the intervention with patients living in urban areas having more to gain of the intervention than rural patients, further investigations is warranted.
label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: Epidemiological studies have repeatedly shown increased occurrence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among people with low socioeconomic status [1, 2] and living in rural areas [3].
label: none

sentence: Primarily due to improved diabetes care, mortality of T2DM patients has decreased substantially in recent decades [4], although this trend has been less favourable among those with low socio-economic status (SES) [5–10].
label: none

sentence: A recent Scandinavian study showed increased mortality among people of low SES, but could not show any systematic differences in mortality between patients living in rural and urban areas [8].
label: none

sentence: Social inequality in mortality and morbidity of patients with T2DM can only be partially explained by differences in the increased incidence of other comorbid disease [1, 11].
label: none

sentence: SES has been reported to influence metabolic control [12], pharmacological treatment [13] and ability to change lifestyle according to the recommendations [14, 15].
label: none

sentence: Inequality in access to and utilization of health care [16, 17] could influence the course of T2DM [18, 19].
label: none

sentence: Though SES and place of living influence care and prognosis of T2DM [8, 10, 11, 20], there is only limited evidence as to whether the effectiveness of diabetes interventions differs with regard to SES and residence.
label: none

sentence: Recent reports suggest that interventions with intensive diabetes care diminish the socio-economic differences in intermediate outcomes [13, 21], but we do not know whether this effect also is seen on long-term outcomes.
label: none

sentence: One may hypothesize, that an intervention with structured personal care may succeed to reduce the difference between socio-demographic groups [13], as the effectiveness of this intervention in two post hoc analyses have been reported to be especially pronounced in women [22] and in patients with severe mental illness [23].
label: none

sentence: Our aim in the present study is to describe how socio-demographic status and residence influences the effectiveness of an intervention with structured personal care in newly diagnosed patients with T2DM regarding all-cause mortality and any diabetes-related endpoint during 19 years of follow-up.
label: none

sentence: The relationship between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users of healthcare services: a cross-sectional study
label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: Frequent users of healthcare services are a vulnerable population that deserves attention due to high costs and negative outcomes such as lower quality of life and higher mortality.
label: none

sentence: Healthcare systems should offer interventions tailored to their needs and to their level of health literacy, including strategies to promote activation.
label: none

sentence: The relationship between health literacy and patient activation remains to be explored.
label: none

sentence: The aim of this study was to examine the association between health literacy and patient activation in a population of frequent users of healthcare services with chronic diseases.
label: none

sentence: Methods
label: none

sentence: Cross-sectional data were collected (before randomization) through a clinical trial evaluating a case management intervention in primary care.
label: none

sentence: Participants (n = 247) were recruited from the list of frequent users of 4 Family Medicine Groups (FMG) in the Saguenay-Lac-St-Jean region of Québec (Canada).
label: none

sentence: They completed questionnaires by self-report during an encounter with a research assistant: (1) the Newest Vital Sign (NVS) to evaluate health literacy (independent variable); and (2) the Patient Activation Measure-13 (PAM-13) to evaluate patient activation (dependent variable).
label: none

sentence: The relationship between health literacy and activation was examined using biserial correlations.
label: none

sentence: Results
label: none

sentence: No association was found between health literacy (independent variable) and patient activation (rb = 0.075, ρ = 0.07) for this population of frequent users of healthcare services.
label: none

sentence: Conclusions
label: none

sentence: This study suggests that there is no relationship between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users of healthcare services.
label: none

sentence: Trial registration
label: none

sentence: Registered October 25, 2012.

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: It is known that 10% of patients use 80% of healthcare system resources [1, 2].
label: none

sentence: These frequent users of services present more chronic conditions, a higher level of psychological distress, as well as increased hospital admissions and mortality rates [3–5].
label: none

sentence: They represent a great challenge for the healthcare system in attempting to optimise care, even more so in a context of chronic disease management.
label: none

sentence: Healthcare systems should offer interventions tailored to their needs [6, 7], including strategies to promote patient activation.
label: none

sentence: According to Hibbard et al., patient activation is defined as “someone’s knowledge, skills, confidence and behaviors needed for self-managing one’s condition or health” [8].
label: none

sentence: They defined four (4) levels of activation: 1) believing the patient role is important, 2) having the confidence and knowledge necessary to take action, 3) actually taking action to maintain and improve one’s health, and 4) staying the course even under stress [9].
label: none

sentence: Although they are related concepts, patient activation is different from patient empowerment, which relates to the process where patients take control of decisions and actions linked to their health [10].
label: none

sentence: High patient activation levels was shown to be associated with better self-management and healthy behaviours [11, 12], better use of screening services and eventually decreased costs for the healthcare system [12].
label: none

sentence: Older age, low level of education or poor income was found to be associated with lower levels of activation [8, 9, 11, 12].
label: none

sentence: Although the operationalization of health literacy is debated, the World Health Organization (WHO) proposes a definition: “the cognitive and social skills which determine the motivation and ability of individuals to gain access to, understand and use information in ways which promote and maintain good health” [13].
label: none

sentence: The National Adult Literacy Survey (NALS) reported that 75% of patients with chronic diseases had limited literacy skills [14].
label: none

sentence: A low level of health literacy would be linked to lower treatment compliance [15, 16] and lower preventive care utilization [17, 18].
label: none

sentence: It was also associated with increased hospital admissions [17, 18], greater risk for poorer health condition [17, 19] and increased mortality [4, 20].
label: none

sentence: Health literacy was raised as an important variable to consider in the management of chronic disease and as a predictor of health condition [21, 22].
label: none

sentence: A few studies have reported a positive association between health literacy and patient activation [23–27].
label: none

sentence: However, many included a sample of patients with higher activation or health literacy levels [23–25] compared to the general population [14].
label: none

sentence: In addition, no study evaluated this association in a population of frequent users of healthcare services with chronic diseases.
label: none

sentence: This association, if present, could prove to be important for care planning for this vulnerable clientele.
label: none

sentence: It would thus be relevant to integrate interventions targeting low health literacy in order to potentially positively impact patient activation.
label: none

sentence: Although frequent users of healthcare services represent an additional challenge for the health care system, no study has examined the potential link between health literacy and activation in this population.
label: none

sentence: The aim of this study was to examine the association between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users of healthcare services with chronic disease in primary care settings.
label: none

label: none

sentence: They provide primary care services and offer extended hours of access through scheduled appointments, walk-in clinics, home care, and telephone access and emergency on-call services.
label: none

sentence: The association between health literacy (independent dichotomic variable, but with the possibility of being a continuous, variable) and patient activation (continuous dependant variable) was examined using biserial correlation.

sentence: Literacy was used dichotomously as adequate literacy (NVS score ≥ 4) or low literacy.
label: none

sentence: Patient activation was used as a continuous variable with the global result.
label: none

sentence: PASW Statistics 20 (SPSS Inc.) was used to perform all analyses with a 5% significance level.
label: none

sentence: Results
label: none

sentence: Table 1 Sample characteristics.
label: none

sentence: Overall, data from 247 participants were included in the analysis (Table 1).
label: none

sentence: Several of these participants (mean age of 60, SD =13 years, 41.6% male) reported high levels of patient activation (level 3, 34.3%; level 4, 30.8%) but a low health literacy level (NVS < 4, 67.5%).
label: none

sentence: Most of the participants had considerable illness burden (DBMA mean 13.4, SD = 8.5) and a high number of chronic diseases (mean of 6).
label: none

sentence: The biserial correlation analysis did not find an association between health literacy and patient activation (rb: 0.075, p = 0.07).
label: none

sentence: Discussion
label: none

sentence: This study examined the relationship between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users of healthcare services with chronic diseases in primary care settings.
label: none

sentence: No association was found.
label: none

sentence: The results of this study are different from others studies evaluating the association between health literacy and patient activation [23–27].
label: none

sentence: A cross-sectional study by Sheikh et al.
label: none

sentence: [26] among adult patients seen at the ER demonstrated an association between health literacy and patient activation, but this association was no longer significant when adjusted for age.
label: none

sentence: Similarly, a study by Gwynn et al.
label: none

sentence: [27] reported an association between health literacy and patient activation, but this association was not significant among patients with low comorbidity (0 or 1 comorbidity).
label: none

sentence: In addition, these studies could be influenced by covariables, such as age [23, 26, 27], ethnicity [24] and education [27].
label: none

sentence: Our study focussed on frequent users of healthcare services with chronic diseases.
label: none

sentence: Their activation and health literacy levels were lower than what was found in previous studies on the subject.
label: none

sentence: This could explain the different results.
label: none

sentence: In light of all these studies, the association between health literacy and patient activation could be present only for certain populations such as older individuals, certain cultural groups or among individuals with high level of activation.
label: none

sentence: More research could examine these hypotheses.
label: none

sentence: The NVS, the TOFHLA, and the S-TOFHLA are all measurement tools validated for health literacy [32, 37, 38], but this is not an easily assessed concept [39] and there is no consensus on any tool [40].
label: none

sentence: The NVS presents the advantage of being available in a French-language version and takes few minutes to complete (3 min).
label: none

sentence: The PAM is a well-recognized tool for measuring patient activation [41].
label: none

sentence: It includes aspects such as knowledge, skills, motivation, and confidence.
label: none

sentence: This study has strengths and certain limits.
label: none

sentence: It is the first study examining the association between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users of healthcare services, and its statistical power was adequate.
label: none

sentence: However, this study presents the secondary analysis of data collected during the RCT mentioned previously.
label: none

sentence: The choice of measurement tools was thus determined before this analysis.
label: none

sentence: Health literacy remains a concept that is difficult to assess and there is no tool universally accepted as the measurement standard [39].
label: limitation

sentence: Using a tool with a broader definition of health literacy, that goes beyond the ability to read and comprehend health information could have yielded different results [42, 43].
label: limitation

sentence: In addition, the questionnaires were self-administered which may have induced a social desirability bias.
label: limitation

sentence: Participants may have answered questions more positively than the reality of their situation.
label: limitation

sentence: Even though we followed current recommendations for the identification of patients [31], the intervention of family physicians in the selection process may have introduced a selection bias.
label: limitation

sentence: However, considering our sample was composed of frequent users, we do not think this had a major impact on our analysis.
label: none

sentence: Although this study did not demonstrate an association, the fact remains that health literacy [17, 18, 40, 44] and patient activation [11, 12] are important concepts for all types of clinicians.
label: none

sentence: Considered separately, health literacy [15, 19] as well as activation [24, 45, 46] have numerous demonstrated impacts on global health.
label: none

sentence: The implementation of interventions for the improvement of patient activation as well as health literacy could be more effective than those focussing only on one of these concepts.
label: none

sentence: Future studies could assess the association between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users in general and not only those presenting chronic diseases.
label: none

sentence: Further research projects could use more than one measure of health literacy simultaneously, for example: the NVS, a validated French-language version of the TOFHLA and/or another measurement tool for health literacy concurrently.
label: none

sentence: A next phase could also detect the effect of time and the intervention on the presence or absence of an association between health literacy and patient activation among frequent users of healthcare services.
label: none

sentence: Conclusions
label: none

sentence: This study did not find an association between health literacy and patient activation in a population of frequent users of healthcare services with chronic diseases in primary care settings.
label: none

sentence: An association between health literacy and patient activation could be present but only for certain populations.
label: none

sentence: Effect of the patient education - Learning and Coping strategies - in cardiac rehabilitation on return to work at one year: a randomised controlled trial show (LC-REHAB)
label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: Personal resources are identified as important for the ability to return to work (RTW) for patients with ischaemic heart disease (IHD) or heart failure (HF) undergoing cardiac rehabilitation (CR).
label: none

sentence: The patient education ‘Learning and Coping’ (LC) addresses personal resources through a pedagogical approach.
label: none

sentence: This trial aimed to assess effect of adding LC strategies in CR compared to standard CR measured on RTW status at one-year follow-up after CR.
label: none

sentence: Methods
label: none

sentence: In an open parallel randomised controlled trial, patients with IHD or HF were block-randomised in a 1:1 ratio to the LC arm (LC plus CR) or the control arm (CR alone) across three Danish hospital units.
label: none

sentence: Eligible patients were aged 18 to ≤60 and had not left the labour market.
label: none

sentence: The intervention was developed from an inductive pedagogical approach consisting of individual interviews and group based teaching by health professionals with experienced patients as co-educators.
label: none

sentence: The control arm consisted of deductive teaching (standard CR).
label: none

sentence: RTW status was derived from the Danish Register for Evaluation of Marginalisation (DREAM).
label: none

sentence: Blinding was not possible.
label: none

sentence: The effect was evaluated by logistic regression analysis and reported as crude and adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence interval (CI).
label: none

sentence: Results
label: none

sentence: The population for the present analysis was N = 244 (LC arm: n = 119 versus control arm: n = 125).
label: none

sentence: No difference in RTW status was found at one year across arms (LC arm: 64.7% versus control arm: 68.8%, adjusted odds ratio OR: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.43-1.31).
label: none

sentence: Conclusion
label: none

sentence: Addition of LC strategies in CR showed no improvement in RTW at one year follow-up.
label: none

label: none

label: none

label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: During the last decades, mortality from ischaemic heart disease (IHD) and heart failure (HF) has decreased due to improved primary and secondary prevention [1–3].
label: none

sentence: Thus, along with changed age composition, many people worldwide are living with these conditions which cause disability on several levels [4, 5].
label: none

sentence: Health promotion and risk factor reduction are typically managed in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) and CR is known to improve clinical outcomes [2].
label: none

sentence: Integrated patient education in CR programmes may also reduce fatal and/or non-fatal cardiovascular events and improve health related quality of life (HRQoL) [3, 6].
label: none

sentence: Patient education is recommended to focus on the individual’s personal resources rather than only increasing knowledge on disease management [7].
label: none

sentence: However, CR interventions have primarily been evaluated on clinical outcomes and less evaluated on the ability to promote level of function including return to work (RTW).
label: none

sentence: Work plays an important role for psychological and social wellbeing, and loss of productivity has economic costs for society [4, 8].
label: none

sentence: Clinical guidelines across nations therefore intend to cover vocational counselling in CR however, RTW internationally still seems to remain suboptimal [9, 10].
label: none

sentence: In Denmark it has been estimated that 21 and 25% of people with IHD and HF, respectively do not RTW 1 year after engaging in CR [11, 12].
label: none

sentence: Moreover, some patients struggle to balance workplace demands with the individual resources and health status and therefore experience recurrent sick leave episodes after RTW [13–15].
label: none

sentence: Problems in the work reintegration process has recently been emphasised since a study showed that detachment from employment was three-fold higher among post myocardial infarct patients 1 year after return to work compared with a matched population [16].
label: none

sentence: Personal resources as coping and self-care are important aspects in a successful RTW process [17].
label: none

sentence: CR-interventions aiming the ability to cope with and engage in everyday life evaluated on RTW have provided inconsistent results [18, 19].
label: none

sentence: Thus, the evidence of the pedagogical approaches and methods to promote the RTW process is unknown.
label: none

sentence: Learning and coping strategies (LC) is a patient education method that aims to facilitate personal resources through inductive teaching with a high level of patient involvement and includes supplement of individual clarifying interviews.
label: none

sentence: The health professionals and experienced patients jointly perform the group based CR sessions [20].
label: none

sentence: The LC-REHAB trial was conducted in a hospital setting in Denmark, and aimed to assess the effect of LC strategies on various outcomes and have shown to promote patient adherence to CR [20, 21].
label: none

sentence: In the present trial it was hypothesised that the LC strategies also promoted RTW compared with usual CR by enabling patients to use acquired LC skills in the RTW process.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, that those receiving LC strategies would reduce the number of sick leave relapses by the gained insight of health condition and how to cope with that.
label: none

sentence: The primary aim was to assess the effect of adding LC strategies in CR on RTW 1 year after inclusion of patients diagnosed with IHD or HF.
label: none

sentence: Secondary to assess if addition of LC strategies in CR reduced sick leave relapses during one-year follow-up.
label: none

sentence: Methods
label: none

sentence: Design
label: none

sentence: The trial was conducted on a subpopulation from the open randomised parallel group controlled trial, LC-REHAB [20].
label: none

sentence: Patients were randomly allocated to the intervention arm (LC strategies in addition to standard CR) or to the control arm (standard CR) in a 1:1 ratio stratified for hospital unit, gender and diagnosis (IHD or HF) in blocks of two to four using a web-based system [20].
label: none

sentence: The allocation procedure was generated independently by the research team.
label: none

sentence: Additional eligibility criteria in the present trial were applied after randomisation to exclude patients assessed with permanent work disability at inclusion.
label: none

sentence: Information on inclusion dates was retrieved from the LC-REHAB trial [20].
label: none

sentence: Follow-up was defined as the week in which the date equivalent to 12 months after inclusion appeared.
label: none

sentence: The trial was conducted and reported according to the CONSORT standards – extension for randomised trials of non-pharmacological treatment [22].
label: none

sentence: Interventions
label: none

sentence: Patients in both arms received a phase II CR program lasting 8 weeks based on the national Danish guidelines on CR starting the first workday after inclusion [20, 23].
label: none

sentence: The programme was delivered in a hospital setting and consisted of group based sessions all lasting 1.5 h with a weekly education session and three exercise sessions per week.
label: none

sentence: The content of the education sessions in both arms were split in eight topics, which were chosen in collaboration with experienced health professionals in CR and experienced patients who previously had undergone CR [20].
label: none

sentence: The topics were: Function and symptoms of the heart, lifestyle effects on the development of IHD and HF, emotional reactions, medication, tiredness, the importance of relatives or other networks, importance and types of exercise, and future life with a chronic disease.
label: none

sentence: The education sessions were primarily managed by a nurse.
label: none

sentence: Exercise sessions consisted of aerobe exercise and muscle strength training managed by a physical therapist.
label: none

sentence: Both arms received CR by the same pair of a nurse and a physiotherapist throughout the CR programme; the pairs were designated to either the intervention or control arm throughout the trial.
label: none

sentence: Due to the nature of the intervention, blinding of health professionals or patients was not possible.
label: none

sentence: Sessions in the two different arms were performed at different times of the day [20].
label: none

sentence: Intervention arm (LC arm)
label: none

sentence: In addition to the described CR intervention, LC strategies took a situated, reflexive, and inductive approach to education and exercise.
label: none

sentence: The rationale behind the pedagogical approach was based on theories behind LC strategies and was described in the initial protocol for the LC-REHAB [20].
label: none

sentence: The rationale was applied through practical implications consisting of: Two individual clarifying interviews (before and after CR), experienced patients as co-educators, material developed for each topic including background literature and questions to facilitate discussions.
label: none

sentence: The approach was ensured by health professionals completing an 8 days competence-education in LC strategies with experienced patients participating the last 4 days, and 1 h evaluation meetings between the pair of health professionals and experienced patient once a week [20].
label: none

sentence: Control arm (standard CR)
label: none

sentence: The CR programme in the control arm was the formerly used in the hospital units (standard CR) [23].
label: none

sentence: The rationale was not described and education and exercise consisted of structured deductive teaching.
label: none

sentence: Identical pre-written, educational slide-shows were used as material for the education sessions.
label: none

label: none

sentence: After trial completion, information on the RTW outcome was retrieved from DREAM, which is administered by The Danish Ministry of Employment [24].
label: none

sentence: The register includes all Danish citizens, who at some point since 1991 have received public benefits.
label: none

sentence: Patients were identified in DREAM by their social security number.
label: none

sentence: Each person is registered once a week with a code representing the type of transfer payment received that particular week [25].
label: none

sentence: For patients to be categorised as having a RTW status (yes) at 1 year follow up, the four consecutive weeks prior to the week of one-year follow up were either codeless (self-support) or had codes representing State Education Fund grants or flexi jobs.
label: none

sentence: For the secondary outcome, each patient was categorised as having an event of RTW during one-year follow up (yes/no).
label: none

sentence: The first event of four consecutive weeks of either self support or codes representing State Education Fund grants or flexi jobs was categorised as RTW (yes).
label: none

sentence: The patients who experienced the event of RTW during follow up but were not registered RTW at 1 year follow up were identified.

sentence: They were referred to as “relapsed patients”.

label: none

sentence: Baseline variables concerning: age, gender, height, weight, diagnosis (IHD or HF), presence of diabetes, smoking, civil status and former participation in CR were reported to dedicated databases in the LC-REHAB trial by the nurses at the CR units [20].
label: none

sentence: At the first CR session, the health professionals handed out self-reported questionnaires for assessing: presence of depression, level of education, and the annual household income [20].
label: none

sentence: Depression (yes/no) was assed by Major Depression Inventory (MDI) [26].
label: none

sentence: Level of education was classified by low, medium, or high.
label: none

sentence: Household income was classified by low, medium, or high.
label: none

sentence: For elaborated classification on level of education and household income, see the initial protocol [20].
label: none

sentence: Since work status prior to CR was assumed associated with RTW, additional information on employment was retrieved from DREAM after allocation to the trial arms [14].
label: none

sentence: No self support prior to CR was dichotomised (yes/no) encompassing whether the patient within 6 months prior to inclusion were self-supported for at least 1 week.

sentence: Statistical methods
label: none

sentence: Descriptive statistics were used to compare the baseline characteristics – Chi-squared for the binary and categorical outcomes, and Studen’s t-test for the continuous.
label: none

sentence: RTW status at 1 year was compared between the two arms using a logistic regression model.
label: none

sentence: The result was presented both as unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence interval (CI).
label: none

sentence: Adjustments were carried out for the stratification variables: gender, cardiac diagnosis and hospital unit.
label: none

sentence: Additional adjustment for age was performed, as age was expected to be associated with RTW [11].
label: none

sentence: To address the secondary aim of the trial, frequencies and percentages described the number of patients who experienced the event of RTW during follow up across trial arms.

label: none

label: none

sentence: Two-hundred-and-forty-four patients were included for the present trial on RTW; 119 and 125 in the LC arm and control arm, respectively.
label: none

label: none

label: none

label: none

sentence: RTW status at one year
label: none

label: none

sentence: No patients died or emigrated during follow up.
label: none

sentence: Regarding the primary outcome, a successful RTW status was observed for 64.7% (95% CI: 55.4- 73.2) in the LC arm, compared with 68.8% (95% CI: 59.9-76.8) in the control arm at 1 year follow up, corresponding to a crude OR 0.83 (95% CI: 0.49-1.42).

sentence: Discussion
label: none

sentence: The present trial showed that addition of LC strategies in hospital based phase II CR did not improve RTW status at one-year follow-up compared to standard CR.
label: none

sentence: Nor did addition of LC strategies seem to reduce sick leave relapses during one-year follow-up.
label: none

sentence: Prior to this trial, comparable CR-interventions aiming at facilitating personal resources to improve RTW had consisted of patient-involving educational sessions, making an individual worksheet plan, including the role of the spouse, shared-decision making and a partnership-based approach [18, 19].
label: none

sentence: The evidence for these approaches and methods is inconsistent and rely on a sparse basis [18, 19].
label: none

sentence: In cancer rehabilitation no comparable educational interventions established effect regarding RTW neither [28].
label: none

sentence: Comparing the effect of patient educational approaches across studies is however complicated by methodical differences as well as heterogeneity in patients, compared interventions and CR-delivery.
label: none

sentence: The trial benefitted from being able to measure the effect of a patient education method developed from a specific pedagogical approach in patient education.
label: none

sentence: Despite the lacking effect of the intervention on RTW, the intervention provides knowledge for further research in CR patient education.
label: none

sentence: According to the first guidance for evaluating complex interventions by the Medical Research Council (MRC), lack of effect may reflect implementation failure rather than genuine ineffectiveness of the intervention and has been identified as problems concerning development, implementation, and evaluation [29].
label: none

sentence: The intervention in the LC arm was developed to aim at promoting the individuals’ personal resources rather than targeting multiple factors affecting level of function [30].
label: none

sentence: A more comprehensive approach has however been suggested with beneficial effects on RTW by both a review on CR and a Cochrane review on cancer rehabilitation [10, 28].
label: none

sentence: LC strategies in this trial lacked of involvement of contextual factors in general and workplaces in particular.
label: none

sentence: The relapsed patients had jobs in health-care, service jobs and manual labour.
label: none

sentence: Job type and support from the employer is found important for CR patients and recently contextual factors at the workplace and organisational practices have been identified to constrain the margin of manoeuvre in work reintegration [15, 31].
label: none

sentence: This may imply that the physical demanding jobs, that also are low level educational job types among relapsed patients are more difficult to reintegrate into after sick leave due to IHD or HF.
label: none

sentence: Thus, the findings in this trial together with emerging evidence suggest development of interventions that foster accommodation and support from involvement of contextual factors like workplaces in integrated CR programmes [31].
label: none

sentence: The implementation of the theoretical understanding in LC strategies may be questioned, since it was not described to what extent the illness perspective on work resumption was approached by the health professionals in the CR sessions.
label: none

sentence: In the present study low household income, low educational level, no self support prior to CR and higher age at baseline were all statistically significant risk factors for not adhering to the CR exercise sessions (results not shown).
label: none

sentence: These socioeconomic factors are in line with frequently reported predictors for not only poor adherence to CR but also detachment from employment [16, 32].
label: none

sentence: It was likely to assume that the poorer adherence in high risk patients contributed to the absent effect of LC strategies.
label: none

sentence: Implementation of future interventions to improve RTW should therefore ensure: adequate RTW-aimed interventions, include practical implications that in particular aim the process of RTW, and optimise adherence to CR for patients in high risk of detachment from employment.
label: none

sentence: Evaluation in this trial was done using an outcome that only accommodated a paid job or education and neglected possible enhanced participation in e.g.
label: none

sentence: volunteer work or social relations.
label: none

sentence: This standardised outcome may have conflicted with the individualised approach in LC strategies.
label: limitation

sentence: Alternative evaluation of CR that measures more participation-related outcome might be relevant to reflect the aim of rehabilitation and furthermore to address the important well-known participation restrictions in patients with chronic IHD [5, 33].
label: none

sentence: Study limitations and strengths
label: none

sentence: Information bias was considered minimal; DREAM has been validated against workplace-registered job attendance and long-term sick listing and found to have high sensitivity and specificity [34].
label: none

sentence: Classification of RTW based on transfer payments from DREAM has elsewhere been defined based on various numbers of weeks (ranging from 1 week to 5 weeks) [12, 13, 16].
label: none

sentence: The chosen definition of four consecutive weeks in this trial might have affected the frequencies of RTW but was not expected to be differentiated between arms.
label: none

sentence: Selection bias was furthermore not considered as there was complete follow up; therefore, threats to the internal validity of the trial were not assumed.
label: none

sentence: The trial was carried out in western Denmark where the population in general is lower educated than the total population of Denmark and the trial enrolled patients with HF [35].
label: limitation

sentence: Both level of education and living with HF are associated with increased risk of not returning to work and may have caused the overall lower RTW proportion (61-73%) in this trial compared to other studies [11, 12, 16].
label: none

sentence: According to the power calculation, a 14% difference in RTW was expected between the two trial arms; however the trial detected a 4 percentage point difference.
label: none

sentence: It was expected that lacking practical implications in the LC strategies for improving RTW rather than a low sample size was the reason of no difference.
label: none

sentence: The estimate may have been affected towards the null hypothesis as mutual interaction between the arms was plausible due to lack of blinding of the health professionals.
label: limitation

sentence: Moreover, patient education was delivered in both arms and the effect of the patient education in the control arm may have contributed to even out the effect of LC strategies.
label: limitation

sentence: Approximately, 50% of the population with IHD and HF asked to participate declined to participate in the trial [21].
label: none

sentence: However, no knowledge of the patients that declined was accessible and it was thus unknown if selection of the patients was present at enrolment.
label: limitation

sentence: This caused limitation of the generalisability of the results and the trial was not able to provide answers about the effect on the total population of people with IHD or HF.
label: limitation

sentence: Temporal and contextual factors affect the ability to RTW and influence the external validity of the outcome measure.
label: limitation

sentence: Also, this means that comparing results in an international context should be done carefully due to heterogeneity in RTW definitions and occupational systems.
label: none

sentence: Conclusion
label: none

sentence: Addition of LC strategies in CR showed no improvement of RTW compared to CR alone after 1 year.
label: none

sentence: Implications for further development and research of patient education methods in CR to improve RTW are: involvement of contextual factors in development of the intervention, and implementation that ensures practical implications targeting RTW like workplace involvement and job type.
label: none

sentence: Lastly, evaluation should address the interventions’ ability to improve participation among patients living with IHD and HF.

sentence: Randomised-controlled trial of a web-based dietary intervention for patients with type 2 diabetes: changes in health cognitions and glycemic control
label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: Increasing prevalence and disease burden has led to an increasing demand of programs and studies focused on dietary and lifestyle habits, and chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
label: none

sentence: We evaluated the effects of a 6-month web-based dietary intervention on Dietary Knowledge, Attitude and Behaviour (DKAB), Dietary Stages of Change (DSOC), fasting blood glucose (FBG) and glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) in patients with uncontrolled HbA1c (> 7.0%) in a randomised-controlled trial (myDIDeA) in Malaysia.
label: none

sentence: Methods
label: none

sentence: The e-intervention group (n = 62) received a 6-month web-delivered intensive dietary intervention while the control group (n = 66) continued with their standard hospital care.
label: none

sentence: Outcomes (DKAB and DSOC scores, FBG and HbA1c) were compared at baseline, post-intervention and follow-up.
label: none

sentence: Results
label: none

sentence: While both study groups showed improvement in total DKAB score, the margin of improvement in mean DKAB score in e-intervention group was larger than the control group at post-intervention (11.1 ± 0.9 vs. 6.5 ± 9.4,p < 0.001) and follow-up (19.8 ± 1.1 vs. 7.6 ± 0.7,p < 0.001), as compared to the baseline.
label: none

sentence: Although there was no significant difference between intervention and control arms with respect to DSOC score and glycaemic control, the e-intervention group showed improved DSOC score (199.7 ± 18.2 vs193.3 ± 14.6,p = 0.046), FBG (7.9 ± 2.5 mmol/L vs. 8.9 ± 3.9 mmol/L,p = 0.015) and HbA1c (8.5 ± 1.8% vs. 9.1 ± 2.0%,p = 0.004) at follow-up compared to the baseline, whereas such improvement was not seen in the control group.
label: none

sentence: Conclusions
label: none

sentence: Most important impact of myDIDeA was on the overall DKAB score.
label: none

sentence: This study is one of the first to demonstrate that an e-intervention can be a feasible method for implementing chronic disease management in developing countries.
label: none

sentence: Concerns such as self-monitoring, length of intervention, intense and individualized intervention, adoption of other domains of Transtheoretical Model and health components, and barriers to change have to be taken into consideration in the development of future intervention programs.
label: none

sentence: Background
label: none

sentence: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is an increasingly important medical and public health issue in many countries, including Malaysia.
label: none

sentence: T2DM is the most common form of diabetes and is characterized by disorders of insulin action and insulin secretion, either of which may be the predominant feature.
label: none

sentence: The latest Malaysian National Health and Morbidity Survey report stated the prevalence of T2DM among adults above 18 years has increased from 11.6% in 2006 to 17.5% in 2015 [1].
label: none

sentence: The increasing prevalence of diabetes and the resulting disease burden has led to a rising demand for evidence-based programs to improve and evaluate diabetes management, especially in developing countries [2].
label: none

sentence: Although T2DM could be inherited, modifiable factors such as body composition and nutrition also play important role in the aetiology of T2DM [3].
label: none

sentence: There is accumulating evidence from a range of different behavioural interventions and delivery methods that have shown promising results in prevention and management of chronic diseases such as T2DM [4].
label: none

sentence: Behavioural interventions have been proven to assist the management of T2DM and websites were found to be a feasible medium for the delivery of such interventions, though the evidence were mostly from Western cultures and did not focus solely on dietary behaviour [5, 6].
label: none

sentence: Instead, dietary behaviour has been a component of a number of web-based studies that aimed at preventing T2DM [7–10].
label: none

sentence: Although limited trials were conducted to test the effectiveness of web-based intervention among T2DM patients, the available evidence has shown an improvement in outcomes for individuals using web-based interventions to increase nutritional knowledge and improve glycaemic control [6, 11].
label: none

sentence: Web-based interventions have demonstrated some favourable outcomes, provided they are further enhanced with appropriate e-research strategies such as use of e-mail or mobile text message reminder to improve log-in rates and use of local languages in content development [5, 12, 13].
label: none

sentence: Interactive components with tracking and personalised feedback, as well as peer-support components were also shown to be effective strategies in ensuring the success of web-based intervention for patients with T2DM [6].
label: none

sentence: The use of Internet has been found to significantly contribute towards improvement of some other health behaviour changes in people with T2DM, especially when the intervention is strengthened with a theoretical framework [14, 15].
label: none

sentence: Theory and evidence-based behaviour interventions are long hailed to be the ideal approach towards successful health behaviour changes.
label: none

sentence: Although no agreement exists as to the best theories for health promotion purposes, the Transtheorical Model (TTM) [16] has become one of the most popular behaviour change models used in health promotion [17].
label: none

sentence: The most commonly applied component of TTM is the construct of Stages of Change (SOC), where the participants are classified into one of the five distinct stages; pre-contemplation, contemplation, preparation, action, and maintenance [18].
label: none

sentence: The TTM and the SOC construct grew on the understanding how people change their behaviour.
label: none

sentence: Few studies have assessed the application of TTM in dietary interventions [14, 19, 20], and more than 75% of studies reviewed by Spencer et al.
label: none

sentence: [14] supported the use of SOC model in dietary interventions.
label: none

sentence: A review of past studies identified various positive impacts of TTM-based dietary interventions, which included reduction of fat consumption, and an increase in the consumption of fruit and vegetables [19].
label: none

sentence: The evidence is particularly strong in patients with T2DM who received intensive intervention of at least 6 months, and the strong evidence substantiates the effectiveness of self-monitoring among others [20].
label: none

sentence: Despite the potential, Lee and colleagues (2015) found lack of exploration on the concurrent use of information technology with TTM [21].
label: none

sentence: To date, there is no published study focused on dietary behaviour change in adults with T2DM via a website-based system.
label: none

sentence: However, dietary modification has been incorporated as a component of a web-based weight-loss program in prevention of T2DM in adults [8].
label: none

sentence: Calorie count as a part of behaviour e-counselling intervention also significantly reduced the weight of the adults at risk for T2DM [9].
label: none

sentence: ICAN, a 12-month RCT which tested the efficacy of physical activity and nutrition behaviour changes in improving diabetes control found favourable results as well [10].
label: none

sentence: Despite the limited evidence, use of Web-based interventions compared to non-web-based interventions showed an improvement in outcomes for individuals using web-based interventions to achieve the specified knowledge and/or behaviour change which include increase in nutritional knowledge and diabetic control [11].
label: none

sentence: A web-based intervention which gives the flexibility for the participants to log in at their own pace and set personalised goals may yield a better and favourable results than generic and non-web-based interventions.
label: none

sentence: Taking these factors into consideration, we aimed to evaluate the effects of myDIDeA ( ala sian  ietary  ntervention for People with Type 2  iabetes: An  - pproach), a 6-month web-based stage-personalised dietary intervention on Dietary Knowledge, Attitude and Behaviour (DKAB), Dietary Stages of Change (DSOC), fasting blood glucose (FBG) and glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) in patients with uncontrolled HbA1c (> 7.0%).
label: none

sentence: We hypothesised myDIDeA to result in significant between- and within-group changes in DKAB, DSOC, FBG and HbA1c in our study population.
label: none

sentence: E-intervention program
label: none

sentence: The development of the dietary intervention program can be described in the following systematic six-step planning approach – 1) needs assessment; 2) module development; 3) development of strategies according to behavioural theory; 4) detailed lesson plans development; 5) implementation of web-based program and 6) effect and process evaluation of the program.
label: none

sentence: Table 2 Sample of the lesson plans.
label: none

sentence: The literature and existing guidelines for patients with T2DM [25–31] were reviewed as part of the needs assessment to identify specific dietary factors of concern.
label: none

sentence: A module consisting of twelve dietary lesson plans were then developed based on the evidence (Table 2).
label: none

sentence: The content of each of the lesson plans was investigated for its relevance to the local community and tailored to suit local context.
label: none

sentence: TTM and SOC constructs [16, 18] were identified to assist with the intervention program design.
label: none

sentence: Program components were developed based on the recommendations, objectives and DSOC.
label: none

sentence: The lesson plans were translated to Bahasa Malaysia, the national language of Malaysia and back translated to English.
label: none

sentence: A working plan of the intervention program that would be delivered via the Internet was then developed and a prototype website was piloted in a small group of patients with T2DM (n = 30) to assess the acceptability and user-friendliness of the intervention structure and web design.
label: none

sentence: The staged-tailored recommendations delivered via the study website (myDIDeA) were aimed to address the barriers and motivate the participants according to their DSOC.
label: none

sentence: The dietary lesson plans in the intervention package was personalised according to the patients’ DSOC and was expected to improve their DKAB and assist them to progress in their respective DSOC.
label: none

sentence: The improvements in DKAB and progress in DSOC were expected to be reflected in the patients’ FBG and HbA1c.
label: none

sentence: Only patients recruited into e-intervention group (n = 66) were provided access to myDIDeA and they were required to login with their unique username and password.
label: none

sentence: Twelve lesson plans were made available to the patients one after another over the period of 6 months, with updates every fortnight.
label: none

sentence: Log-in reminders were sent via e-mail each time myDIDeA is updated with new lesson plans and participants were followed-up with text messages if they failed to log-in within three days post-update.
label: none

sentence: The participants were also encouraged to send their queries to the study nutritionist via the website.
label: none

sentence: The effectiveness of the web-delivered intervention program was evaluated via the randomised-controlled trial.
label: none

sentence: Process evaluation in form of intervention adherence and program reception were conducted at post intervention.
label: none

sentence: On average, each participant logged in at least once for each lesson plan and spent almost 12 min on the site.
label: none

sentence: The participants’ content satisfaction, acceptability, and usability scores were satisfactory.
label: none

sentence: A detailed description of the development and process evaluation of the e-intervention program has been published previously [32].

sentence: Measures
